plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white flowers with delicate green-tipped inner petals push up through frost and leaf litter. They carpet woodlands, churchyards and old gardens in drifts of snowy white, often the first sign that winter is loosening its grip.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, sometimes starting as early as December
plants.location: United Kingdom and temperate Europe, in woodlands and gardens
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein and heat-generating tissue that lets them melt their way through snow. Their bulbs are also the original source of galantamine, a compound used in medicine.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: This small tree covers bare branches with fragrant blossoms while snow can still lie on the ground. The scent is sweet and spicy, and the flowers have long been celebrated in poetry and painting across East Asia as a symbol of endurance and the coming spring.
plants.location: Japan and the Yangtze River region of China
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. The fruit is pickled into umeboshi and steeped into umeshu, a sweet plum liqueur.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A glossy evergreen shrub that lights up the late-winter garden with large, rose-like blooms. Its flowers, often double and up to five inches across, show off bold blushes of pink, red and white against dark, polished leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Temperate gardens in East Asia, where it is native, and the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Thousands of cultivars have been bred over centuries, with flower shapes ranging from simple singles to formal doubles.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise from strappy green leaves and carry large globes of trumpet-shaped flowers in vivid blue and violet. In the height of summer they bring cool color to sunny borders and coastal slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (December to February)
plants.location: Southern Hemisphere summer gardens, including Australia, and its native South Africa
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for love and flower, and it is a popular and hardy garden plant in warm climates.
